rationale: Lycopolitan ⲝⲁⲥⲓϩⲏⲧ = Sahidic ϫⲁⲥⲓ-ϩⲏⲧ 'high-of-heart' = haughtiness, arrogance. Paired with σπαταλία 'luxury' as moral-vice doublet.
Greek loanword σπαταλία (cf. 1 Tim 5:6, James 5:5) — wanton, luxurious living as moral vice. Standard NT/early Christian register.
Greek loanword πλατύνω 'widen, spread, enlarge' (cf. Matt 23:5, 2 Cor 6:11). Used here in cosmic-architectural context.
Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲡⲱϭ/ⲡⲱϭⲉ 'split, break asunder, shatter.' Used qualitatively of the archons broken in the war.
Lycopolitan/Coptic ⲏⲡⲣⲉ 'fruit, produce' — agricultural noun. Here 'their fruits dried up' (ⲁ ⲛⲟⲩⲙ̄ⲡⲣⲉ ⲃⲱϣ).
Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲱⲱϣ 'be dry, withered.' Agricultural verb fitting the fruit-context.
Lycopolitan ϩⲱⲕ = Sahidic ϩⲱⲕ 'strip, despoil.' Used of Jesus the Glorious stripping the archontic host of its captive light — redemptive plunder.
Ordinal series of cosmic battles: third war = Third Ambassador's revelation; fourth war = Jesus the Glorious One's redemptive battle. Standard Manichaean structuration of cosmogonic combats.
Greek-derived feminine substantivized adjective ἀρχοντική (sc. δύναμις or στρατιά) — collective for the archonic host/forces of darkness. Standard Manichaean usage.
Coptic verbal noun ⲕⲱⲧ 'build' substantivized = 'building, structure.' Cosmological term for the established cosmic edifice. Distinguished from homophonous 'pluck' (ⲕⲱⲧϩ) and 'circuit' (ⲕⲱⲧⲉ).
